text:
SOURCE-ASSISTED IMAGE READING, 22 September 2026

Base: review-2026-09-22-image-only. The base is preserved unchanged. This reader has now seen the earlier fragment report, edition OCR, and print images. None of the following is an independent image-only reading.

Coverage and physical lines:
The base image image-001.png is the upper 310 native pixels of the manuscript region 560,1260,1020,560 on canvas 0. Its rows 1–7 correspond to the first seven rows of F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg. Rows 1 and 7 are clipped in the base. Below, rows are counted from each named crop's top, including partial rows. Overlapping rows are the same text, not additional manuscript lines. Parentheses propose expansions, ? marks uncertainty, and [illegible] is unresolved image text. ul' is retained rather than silently expanded to vel.

F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:3 [Q]uerelam. Remou[illegible]. sed
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:3-right ¶ [illegible]
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:4 quo? potuit h(oc) peti cu(m) nemo sin(e) accusatore
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:5 p(ro)hibeatur? ab honore. ff. de mun'. et ho. Rescripto.
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:6 §. si quis. e(rgo) multo forcius remoueri ab honore
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:7 sin(e) accusatore nō d(ebet)? ul' saltim sin(e) inquisitio(n)e ul'
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:8 denu(n)ciatione de q(ui)b(us) mo(dis) h(ab)es. s. de accu. sup(er) hiis.
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:9 R(espo)n. p(re)dicta iura et modi p(re)dicti locu(m) h(ab)ent ubi de cri-
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:10 mine agitur. hic aut(em) nō remouet(ur) p(ro)pter crim(en) s(ed) quia
F-o1p7_c0_560_1260_1020x560.jpg:11 ius nō h(ab)et in eccl(es)ia et h(ab)es simile [illegible]

F-o1p7_c0_560_1780_1020x560.jpg:6 [D]e nouo. pone q(uod) p(er) annu(m) unu(m) ul' plures
F-o1p7_c0_560_1780_1020x560.jpg:7 semel ul' bis omisi pete(re) pensione(m) solita(m)
F-o1p7_c0_560_1780_1020x560.jpg:8 ul' omisi int(er)esse electio(n)i nu(m)q(ui)d p(ro)pter h(oc) amitto possessio(n)e(m) iur(is) p(er)-
F-o1p7_c0_560_1780_1020x560.jpg:9 cipiendi et eligendi. R(espo)n. nō cu(m) possessio sine
F-o1p7_c0_560_1780_1020x560.jpg:10 a(n)i(m)o nō amittat(ur). ff. de acquir. pos. [illegible]

These two passages are source-assisted and partially uncertain even where the edition supplies a plausible word. The De nouo sequence is clear enough for identification; its abbreviation expansions are interpretive. No accuracy percentage is claimed.

Corrections to base and previous report:
The decorated Q belongs to Querelam on row 3, not the first word on row 4. The base's causā?/Remotā?, priuatio?, and ab illo? are not retained. The red mark in row 3-right is a pilcrow-like sign; the following word remains unread. Print reads Removeri as the lemma, but the manuscript's corresponding word is not fully resolved. The former report's A27 remoueri should not be treated as certain: p(ro)hibeatur? is a better current candidate, matching print prohibeat(ur). Print has ut removeatur / sine accusatione; manuscript seems remoueri / sine accusatore, with a further abbreviated negative expression. Do not replace the manuscript with the print.

Other image checks:
F-o1p7_c0_560_220_1020x560.jpg, opening eleven visible rows: checked against print n125 lower right. The opening question and the sequence electionem prepositi / postulationem cassauit / excessus postulantium / non citato / in notoriis / citatio support the same passage. No new full transcription of these rows is supplied.
F-o1p7_c0_1620_1780_600x560.jpg and F-o1p7_c0_1620_2300_600x560.jpg: inspected the right-column transition and the following discussion. These are trimmed and faint. The earlier assertion that the large initial spells Petebat is not verified; leave the exact manuscript lemma unresolved. Print n127 certainly has Substractum followed by Quesiui qualiter amittitur possessio iuris eligendi. No lost right-hand wording has been supplied as manuscript text.
full.jpg: inspected for layout only; two columns, right column trimmed. No full-leaf transcription or collation was undertaken.

Actual comparison sources:
Paris 1516 Lectura aurea in primum librum Decretalium, Internet Archive bub_gb_3RhpO70ZNiwC. Cached OCR bern.txt lines 17950–18350 read; downloaded DjVu XML used to locate page n126. Print images n125 (55v), n126 (56r, printed Fo. lvi), and n127 (56v) inspected at original detail. Scoped print comparisons: n125 right column from Duximus confirmandam; n126 left column Querelam/Removeri and De novo; n127 left column Substractum/Quesiui. Neighboring print matter was visible but not fully collated.

Also read: previous F-o1p7 report; IA bibliographic metadata; cached Bibliotheca Augustana X 1.6 text search excerpts for Bonae memoriae and Querelam (underlying decretals, not evidence for the commentary's attribution).

Conclusion: identified, high identification confidence, as the text printed under Bernardus Compostellanus in the Lectura aurea, on X 1.6.23–24. Sustained connecting prose in the opening argument, Querelam, and De novo agrees in sequence, beyond the shared decretal lemmata. This does not establish an authorial recension, historical originality, manuscript date/provenance, or witness novelty. The passages had already been compared in the earlier report; these are additional scoped checks, not held-out evidence.
